## Trial `default-deny-baseline-ubuntu24__fu2ppTw`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The core task outcome — opening exactly one node2->node3 TCP/8080 path through node1 while leaving all other lan-a<->lan-b traffic refused — is directly demonstrated by pf ruleset inspection and functional connectivity tests, both before and after full one-at-a-time restarts of all three nodes. Boot-identity changes for node1 (kern.boottime), node2, and node3 (boot_id) are corroborated by the fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot, and post-restart behavior (pass/refuse pattern, interface/route persistence) matches the pre-restart baseline, so the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol is well-supported for all three nodes even though restart persistence was not itself part of the public task contract. Minor hygiene residue (a leftover nc test listener and log file on node3, and an uncleaned early troubleshooting attempt) slightly lowers the hygiene score but does not affect functional correctness.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Open exactly one path: node2 (lan-a) can reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP port 8080 through node1
  - **Why:** node1's pf ruleset shows exactly one added pass rule ("pass in quick on vtnet1 inet proto tcp from (vtnet1:network) to (vtnet2:network) port = http-alt") layered on top of the existing default-deny (cmd-ac73f229c4db4b57). Functional tests confirm node2->node3:8080 succeeds and actually delivers application data (cmd-c4bfd042c95540c2, cmd-a0f46cd1daf84f41, cmd-8384360c226f4efa), both before and after node1's restart (cmd-6526db564f3c415b, cmd-b307b826f2c24131/cmd-8f08b4c5558b4d5f).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ac73f229c4db4b57`, `cmd-c4bfd042c95540c2`, `cmd-a0f46cd1daf84f41`, `cmd-8384360c226f4efa`, `cmd-6526db564f3c415b`, `cmd-b307b826f2c24131`, `cmd-8f08b4c5558b4d5f`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Every other flow between lan-a and lan-b remains refused (default-deny preserved, no unintended openings)
  - **Why:** node2->node3:22 and ICMP both node2->node3 and node3->node2 all time out / are refused, both immediately after rule application and after every node's restart (cmd-a0f46cd1daf84f41, cmd-8384360c226f4efa, cmd-6526db564f3c415b, cmd-1bfb6a8cfd044975, cmd-b307b826f2c24131). The full pf rule dump (cmd-ac73f229c4db4b57) shows only the single new pass rule added on top of the interface-scoped block-drop rules that already denied lan-a<->lan-b traffic, with no other pass rules touching opt1/opt2 traffic.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ac73f229c4db4b57`, `cmd-a0f46cd1daf84f41`, `cmd-8384360c226f4efa`, `cmd-6526db564f3c415b`, `cmd-1bfb6a8cfd044975`, `cmd-b307b826f2c24131`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.720**. Most state-changing actions were purposeful (interface/IP assignment on node1/node2/node3 as a necessary prerequisite for the two LANs to reach each other via node1; the single pf pass rule; restart-protocol commands). A few issues remain: (1) an nc listener bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 was left running on node3 after task completion (started at cmd-636de900dfa74de7 and restarted post-reboot at cmd-c3e8f46906d94774), visible in the after_executor snapshot as a retained listening socket — this is test scaffolding, not part of the task's intended service, and was not torn down; its accompanying /tmp/nc8080.log is also left behind. (2) An early misconfigured firewall-rule XML edit (cmd-0cc744ba4f6146ff, destination network 'opt2ip') was corrected by restoring the pre-edit backup and reapplying (cmd-1814ff84a7af4147) — a legitimate corrective action, not penalized. (3) A failed 'configctl system configure' background attempt (cmd-e3b20e5adb3640de) produced a log file that was subsequently removed (cmd-45ba3b6aa6004393), and diagnostic tcpdump captures were read-only/bounded and killed afterward (cmd-45ba3b6aa6004393). No failed services, no destructive actions, no weakened security controls, and the default-deny posture was preserved throughout.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-636de900dfa74de7`, `cmd-c3e8f46906d94774`, `global:after_executor:node3:listening-sockets`, `cmd-0cc744ba4f6146ff`, `cmd-1814ff84a7af4147`, `cmd-e3b20e5adb3640de`, `cmd-45ba3b6aa6004393`
